_comment: The publication set a release MUST contain, recorded the way api/*.api records the
ABI: a committed expectation that drift is checked against in BOTH directions.
Why a recorded list and not a derived one: gradle.properties sets
kotlin.native.ignoreDisabledTargets=true, so a target that cannot be built on the
publishing host is SKIPPED SILENTLY -- its publish task and its artifacts both
disappear together. Anything derived from the Gradle model at release time would
shrink with the loss and still pass. Only an independent record catches it.
The publish job runs on ubuntu-latest and the Apple klibs cross-compile there; that
is exactly the property most likely to regress on a Kotlin upgrade, and the failure
mode is a beta that ships without iOS while every gate stays green.
Changing this list is a deliberate release-shape decision: update it in the same
commit as the target change, and say so in CHANGELOG.md.
